notes:
Three real rungs in four bullets. Bullet 3 ('Mining points in Morimar Basalt Fields are located across the map') is not an action -- it is where bullet 2 happens -- so it merges into the mining step rather than becoming a rung of its own.

The twelve grid refs under the 'Location of known mining points' section are NOT twelve steps. They are twelve places one unnamed object may be, only one or two of which are up at a time, so they are a note on step 2 and the step keeps a null grid. Compare An Explorer's Footsteps, where seventeen monuments each really were a separate visit in a fixed set: here you mine ONE nugget at whichever point happens to be up. The page never names the mining point entity either, so the target is none.

The Pickaxe comes from 'Quest Reqs' and is genuinely something you must hold to mine, so it is modelled as items, with the two Bayld pickaxes Floralie sells as independent alternatives -- both resolve. Ionis and mining fatigue are advice.

The page says outright that the nugget may be mined BEFORE flagging the quest. That is safe here: accepting the quest is already evidence step 1 is done, so holding a nugget lands the mark on Apolliane for the trade, which is exactly right.

steps.note: mine it yourself -- the page is explicit that a bought or traded nugget will not do. Known points, one or two up at a time: (H-5), (H-7/8), (G-6), (F-6), (F-8), (E-9), (F-10), (F-9), (I-9), (J-6), (J-10), (J-11); the last needs no walk past Bedrock Crags. Ionis reduces Adoulin mining fatigue.

notes:
Both key items must be written WITH their literal double quotes -- res/key_items.lua 2352 and 2353 really are named '"Ephemeral Endeavor"' and '"Enlightened Endeavor"', and they resolve only in that form. Unquoted they return no id, which would have cost this quest both of its evidence points. The wiki writes them with the quotes too, so this is the page's own spelling, not a repair.

Bullet 1 spans two zones -- talk in Eastern Adoulin, then travel to Rala Waterways -- so it splits, and the travel half merges into the Yeggha Dolashi visit rather than becoming a bare zone rung: she stands at the destination, so her marker already points there. The door behind her is real but the page never names it, so it stays in the note instead of becoming an unnamed, unmarkable rung between two things you actually do.

Zurko-Bazurko and Sverdheid are two fights inside one battlefield and stay two steps; only the second is observable. The page writes the second as 'Sverdheid ???' -- recorded as Sverdheid, because monsters are matched live by name and '???' would never match.

'Rune Fencer Level 66+' in Quest Reqs is BOTH gates. The 'Notes' section is a prerequisite shortcut and a re-challenge price; neither is a step.

Bullets 6 and 7 are the SAME ??? at Crawlers' Nest map 2 (I-10), examined twice about a minute apart. A ??? can never carry a marker and neither examination is observable, so two rungs there would be noise the player cannot be tracked through; they merge, the way Divine Might's double examination does.

The boots are bought with the watch and both boots and blood are consumed by the burial, so nothing survives to the end -- flagged consumed_key_item. notes:
Started by ZONING, not by talking: bullet 1 says entering Qulun Dome is what gives the cutscene, and Raptorlegs Gedwad is described as stuck at the entrance. The header's giver is kept in start.raw and as start.npc -- he is a real standing entity, unlike the cutscene-only givers the pilot hit -- but step 1 is a travel, and it is placed at Beadeaux (H-7), which is the side of the boundary the player has to walk to and the only grid the page gives. Steps 7 to 10 are inside Qulun Dome: bullet 10's 'Zone out of Qulun Dome' settles that the Beastmen's Banner at (F-8) is in the dome, not in Beadeaux.

Bullet 5 is a real step -- synthesize the Barbut -- but its recipe was stripped by the prepass, which is why the step carries the Quadav Parts it consumes and nothing more.

Da'Vhu's Barbut is obtained at step 10 and needed at step 11, and it is deliberately NOT evidence: it is in the header's Reward, and because this quest is REPEATABLE a returning player still wearing it would have the mark jump straight to the last rung on re-flagging. That is precisely the failure rule 7 exists to prevent, so steps 10 and 11 fall back on the session latch.

Bullet 7 spawns seven NMs but only Diamond Quadav must die -- the rest despawn with him -- so the fight step names only him as a kill and the other six ride on the examine as spawns. The 10,000 gil at bullet 3 cannot be expressed as an item and is a note; so is the next-game-day wait at bullet 4 and the Conquest Tally lockout if you decline.

notes:
Fame 'OT' gates nothing and the region is null. tools/lib/normalize.lua aliases the raw value 'ot' to 'other' and maps 'other' to false, so resolve.lua returns no region for it; the wiki's shorthand for Norg fame is 'N', which does resolve. The draft read OT as an Outlands/Tenshodo abbreviation for Norg fame -- plausible, and the five OT pages really do all start in Norg, but it is an inference the pipeline's own canonical table contradicts, and AUTHORING.md is explicit that a Fame value outside the nine names is region null. raw is kept verbatim. FLevel 1 is the floor anyway, so nothing changes behaviourally either way.

The ferry is the reason this is medium. Bullets 6 to 8 happen aboard the Mhaura-Selbina ferry, which the page names only in those words; it never gives the zone the game uses, so the Enagakure fight has a null zone rather than a name I would have had to supply myself. Nothing is lost by that -- monsters are matched live in whatever zone you are standing in -- but the step cannot be placed.

Three consecutive rungs on Leodarion (talk, trade, talk again next day) collapse to one marker, which is fine; they stay three because the trade and the day boundary are real and the last one is the only observable thing in the middle of this quest. The Ninja Hakama at bullet 9 is the header's Reward, so the closing step carries no evidence and the quest ends on a dockside cutscene rather than a hand-in. The night-time sailing window and the Vana'diel day wait are both invisible to the addon.

notes:
Klara is in the header and appears NOWHERE in the walkthrough. The quest actually opens by zoning into Bastok Markets (S) from North Gustaberg (S), and every interaction afterwards is with Gentle Tiger or Blatherix. I kept her as start.npc because she is at (H-6), the same corner as Gentle Tiger, so the pre-flag marker still points a player at the right place -- but step 1 is the zone entry, and the disagreement is flagged rather than smoothed over. Medium for that.

Bullet 3 says 'in any order' outright, so Paul, Biggorf and Wilhelmina share a group and all three draw at once; a strict ladder would mark Paul and then nothing until you happened to walk past him. Bullet 5's sub-bullet -- talk to all three MORE if Blatherix gives no cutscene -- is the same three NPCs again and is a note on the Blatherix step, not a second group.

Nothing in this quest is observable. Not one step grants a key item or an item, so every evidence field is null, and that is the honest answer rather than reaching for the three trade goods. I deliberately did NOT add an 'obtain the ingredients' rung: the Mess Tin, Mushpot and Twinkle Powder are all Auction House or vendor stock, a player may be holding them from the start, and evidence on them would jump the mark past six rungs of cutscenes. They stay as items on the trade, where readiness already looks ahead.

The Elixir from Blatherix after Burden of Suspicion is a latent precondition for bullet 1's cutscene with nothing observable behind it, and the pre-quest 'wait one game day and re-zone after Fire in the Hole' notice is a gate the addon cannot see. Steps 7 and 8 are consecutive on Blatherix and collapse to one marker.

notes:
Five bullets, three of which are route advice, and the whole quest is one cutscene, one walk and one battlefield.

Grid conflict, kept rather than reconciled: the header puts Ratihb at Aht Urhgan Whitegate (J-12), bullet 1 puts the Shararat Teahouse at (K-12). start keeps the header's, step 1 keeps the walkthrough's. The walkthrough names no NPC at all -- only the teahouse -- so the target is the header's Ratihb, which is a real standing entity; if the live trigger turns out to be walking into the teahouse rather than talking to him, the step loses nothing but its marker.

The object name is the other reason for medium. Bullet 2 calls the ship 'the The Ashu Talif', bullets 3 and 4 call it 'the Cutter'. I used Cutter, because that is what the two INSTRUCTION bullets say, and left Ashu Talif for the battlefield zone, which resolves only with its article. If the live entity is named Ashu Talif instead, step 3 keeps its rung and loses its marker.

The Life float is step 1's evidence and step 3's requirement -- a key item can be both, the duplicate gate is about evidence only. Bullet 5 is an outcome, not a hand-in: the reward arrives with the post-fight cutscene and there is no NPC to return to, so the ladder ends on the fight. Leleroon's artifact commissioning under bullet 1 is a separate reward track and the transcluded section is not available, so neither becomes a step.
